S0.label: Onboarding
S0.explain: Getting a repo ready so agents can work on it safely.

S1.label: Intake
S1.explain: The factory reads the request, checks for duplicates, picks a track and asks questions.

S2.label: Research
S2.explain: An agent studies the code and docs and lays out the options.

S3.label: Spec
S3.explain: An agent writes what will change and the acceptance tests that prove it.

S4.label: Design
S4.explain: An agent writes the design, contracts, data changes and risks.

S5.label: Plan
S5.explain: The work is split into parts, ordered and given a budget.

S6.label: Build
S6.explain: A coding agent writes the code in a locked-down sandbox and opens a draft PR.

S7.label: Verify
S7.explain: The factory checks the PR (tests, spec, secrets, rules) and signs the evidence.

S8.label: Review and merge
S8.explain: A code owner reviews the PR; a person merges it on GitHub.

S8a.label: Merge
S8a.explain: The approved PR is merged on GitHub by a person, and re-checked if the base moved.

S8b.label: Release
S8b.explain: The merged change is deployed, if this project releases through the factory.

S9.label: Close
S9.explain: The requester accepts the result and the factory records what it learned.

0.1.label: Read-only scan
0.1.explain: The factory and the onboarding agent read the repo: owners, tests, security, settings.

0.2.label: Small-changes review
0.2.explain: The agent checks the repo facts and agent instructions needed for small changes.

0.3.label: Full-work review
0.3.explain: The agent maps the code, drafts specs and locks the acceptance tests needed for all work.

0.4.label: Controls and people
0.4.explain: GitHub protections are read and who decides what is set.

0.5.label: Sign-off
0.5.explain: A person signs off the onboarding.

1.1.label: Read the request
1.1.explain: The request is cleaned up and marked as untrusted input.

1.2.label: Check for duplicates
1.2.explain: The factory looks for the same or conflicting requests.

1.3.label: Pick a track
1.3.explain: An agent sizes the work; the factory picks the track from the rules.

1.4.label: Check eligibility
1.4.explain: The factory checks this repo is ready for this track.

1.5.label: Ask questions
1.5.explain: An agent asks what is unclear and writes the agreed goal.

1.6.label: Mark ready
1.6.explain: The requester says the request is ready to be accepted.

2.1.label: Study the code
2.1.explain: An agent reads the relevant code and docs at the current commit.

2.1b.label: Dig deeper
2.1b.explain: An agent reverse-engineers an unclear area.

2.2.label: Find impact
2.2.explain: An agent lists what and who the change affects.

2.3.label: Lay out options
2.3.explain: An agent writes the options and a decision brief.

2.4.label: Elaborate the initiative
2.4.explain: Large initiatives only: an agent breaks the goal down.

2.5.label: Final goal sign-off
2.5.explain: Large initiatives only: a person accepts the goal for good.

3.1.label: Find affected requirements
3.1.explain: An agent finds which existing requirements change.

3.2.label: Draft the spec change
3.2.explain: An agent writes the change to the spec.

3.3.label: Validate the spec
3.3.explain: The factory checks the spec is complete and consistent.

3.4.label: Write acceptance criteria
3.4.explain: An agent writes the tests that will prove the change.

3.5.label: Independent spec review
3.5.explain: A second agent with fresh context reviews the spec.

4.1.label: Decisions
4.1.explain: An agent records the design decisions.

4.2.label: Contracts
4.2.explain: An agent writes interface contracts; the factory checks them.

4.3.label: Data and migrations
4.3.explain: An agent writes the data and migration plan.

4.4.label: Risks and operations
4.4.explain: An agent writes performance, security and operations notes.

4.5.label: Factory rules check
4.5.explain: The design is checked against the factory rules.

4.6.label: Design review
4.6.explain: A person reviews the design and threats.

5.1.label: Split into parts
5.1.explain: An agent splits the work into parts that can be built separately.

5.2.label: Order the parts
5.2.explain: An agent decides which part goes first.

5.3.label: Task list per part
5.3.explain: An agent writes the task list for each part.

5.4.label: Link the tests
5.4.explain: Each part is linked to the tests that prove it.

5.5.label: Set the budget
5.5.explain: The factory works out the budget for each part.

5.6.label: Check capacity
5.6.explain: The factory checks there is room to build.

5.7.label: Schedule
5.7.explain: A person or the factory schedules the build.

6.0.label: Start building
6.0.explain: The factory gives the part a coding slot and budget.

6.1.label: Prepare the sandbox
6.1.explain: A clean sandbox is made from the approved commit.

6.2.label: Run tests first
6.2.explain: The existing tests are run before any change.

6.3.label: Confirm new tests fail
6.3.explain: The new acceptance tests are run and must fail first.

6.4.label: Write the code
6.4.explain: The coding agent works through the task list.

6.5.label: Self-check
6.5.explain: The factory checks the change against the scope, budget and safety rules.

6.6.label: Open draft PR
6.6.explain: The factory bot opens or updates the draft PR.

7.1.label: Build and tests
7.1.explain: Build, lint and the full test suite on the PR's commit.

7.2.label: Test integrity
7.2.explain: Tests were not weakened and the acceptance tests are real.

7.3.label: Matches the spec
7.3.explain: The change does what the approved spec says.

7.4.label: Secrets and dependencies
7.4.explain: No new secret and no unapproved dependency.

7.5.label: Factory rules
7.5.explain: The change follows the factory rules.

7.6.label: Sign the evidence
7.6.explain: The factory signs the evidence pack for this exact commit.

8.1.label: Code review
8.1.explain: A code owner reviews the PR.

8.2.label: Merge on GitHub
8.2.explain: A person merges the PR on GitHub; the factory never merges.

S8b.label: Release
S8b.explain: The change is deployed after release approval.

9.2.label: Requester accepts
9.2.explain: The requester checks the result does what they asked.

9.3.label: Close-out record
9.3.explain: The factory writes the final record of the item.

9.4.label: Learn
9.4.explain: The factory proposes improvements from finished work.

9.5.label: Spot-check audit
9.5.explain: A person audits a sample of lightly reviewed merges.

G0.label: Accept the request
G0.explain: Decide whether the factory should take this request on.

G1.label: Confirm the goal
G1.explain: Agree what the request is for, before the factory studies it.

G1f.label: Final goal sign-off
G1f.explain: Large initiatives only: accept the goal after it has been worked out.

G2.label: Approve the spec
G2.explain: Approve what will change and the acceptance criteria.

G3.label: Approve the plan
G3.explain: Approve the full plan for this exact commit.

G3d.label: Approve the design
G3d.explain: Approve the design and the risks it names.

G3s.label: Approve the outline
G3s.explain: Approve how the work is split into parts and ordered.

G3o.label: Approve test changes
G3o.explain: The acceptance tests differ from the approved criteria; approve the difference.

G4.label: Code review
G4.explain: A code owner approves the PR. Always required.

G5.label: Approve the release
G5.explain: Approve deploying the merged change. Needs "confirm it's you".

G6.label: Accept the result
G6.explain: The requester says the change does what they asked.

X1.label: Allow irreversible action
X1.explain: The agent wants to do something that cannot be undone.

X2.label: Allow protected-file change
X2.explain: The change touches files only people may change.

X3.label: Allow new dependency
X3.explain: The change adds a new package.

X4.label: Review a bypassed merge
X4.explain: Someone merged without the factory's check; review it after the fact.

E1.label: Allow a lighter track
E1.explain: Move the work to a track with fewer steps.

E2.label: Allow a rule exception
E2.explain: The work breaks a factory rule; allow it once or not.

E3.label: Allow more budget
E3.explain: The work needs more budget than planned.

E4.label: Choose what happens next
E4.explain: The agents are stuck; choose to resume, re-plan, take over or stop.

E5.label: Override an escalation
E5.explain: Decide an overdue approval on someone else's behalf.

E6.label: Change a locked test
E6.explain: A locked acceptance test must change; approve the change.

M1.label: Approve a settings change
M1.explain: Approve a change to the factory's or a project's settings.

M2.label: Approve a rule variance
M2.explain: Let one project differ from a standard rule.

M3.label: Approve a process change
M3.explain: Change the standard tracks, steps or limits.

M4.label: Sign off onboarding
M4.explain: Confirm the repo is ready for the level asked. Needs "confirm it's you".

M5.label: Raise agent autonomy
M5.explain: Let agents do more on this project with less review.

M6.label: Grant approver rights
M6.explain: Let a person decide approvals they could not before.

Q1.label: Security hold
Q1.explain: Work stopped because an agent did something unsafe.

SECT.label: Security review
SECT.explain: A security approver decides if the hold was real before anything else happens.

stage.label: Step approval
stage.explain: An approval on the normal path of the work.

action.label: Risky action approval
action.explain: An approval for one risky action.

exception.label: Exception approval
exception.explain: An approval for leaving the normal rules.

meta.label: Factory change approval
meta.explain: An approval for changing how the factory works.

quarantine.label: Security approval
quarantine.explain: An approval after a security hold.

g0g1.label: Accept and confirm goal
g0g1.explain: Switch "Accept the request" and "Confirm the goal" on or off together.

g2.label: Spec approval
g2.explain: Switch "Approve the spec" on or off.

g3d.label: Design approval
g3d.explain: Switch "Approve the design" on or off.

g3_g3s.label: Plan approval
g3_g3s.explain: Switch "Approve the outline" and "Approve the plan" on or off together.

g5.label: Release approval
g5.explain: Switch "Approve the release" on or off.

g6.label: Result acceptance
g6.explain: Switch "Accept the result" on or off.

request_changes.label: Request changes
request_changes.explain: Send it back with what must change; the agent tries again.

reject.label: Reject
reject.explain: Say no; the work stops or goes back as the rules say.

supersede.label: Replaced
supersede.explain: A newer version replaced this one before it was decided.

expire.label: Expired, not approved
expire.explain: Nobody decided in time; expiry never approves.

withdraw.label: Withdrawn
withdraw.explain: The request or approval was withdrawn.

reason.label: Reason
reason.explain: Why you decided this; saved with your decision.

step_up.label: Confirm it's you
step_up.explain: Sign in again with your security key before this decision.

two_person.label: Needs two people
two_person.explain: Two different people must approve this.

sod_waiver.label: Single-approver exception
sod_waiver.explain: You decided your own request because you are the only person who can. Recorded.

admin_override.label: Decide as factory admin
admin_override.explain: You are deciding outside the normal rules. Your name and reason are recorded.

ask_for_work.label: Ask for work
ask_for_work.explain: Send a request to the factory.

hand_back.label: Hand back
hand_back.explain: Give the work back to the agents.

mark_done.label: Mark my work done
mark_done.explain: Tell the factory your human-led work is ready to be checked.

unsure.label: I'm not sure
unsure.explain: Ask a code owner to do a full review instead.

always_required.label: Always required
always_required.explain: No project can switch this approval off.

switched_off.label: Off: step skipped
switched_off.explain: This approval does not exist on this project; nothing is approved automatically.

decided_together.label: Decided together
decided_together.explain: Several approvals shown and decided as one card when one person holds them all.

superseded.label: Replaced
superseded.explain: A newer version replaced it before a decision.

expired.label: Expired, not approved
expired.explain: Nobody decided in time. Nothing was approved.

closed.label: Closed
closed.explain: The work ended, so the approval closed.

feasible.label: Can be decided
feasible.explain: Whether someone holds the right to decide this approval.

infeasible.label: Nobody can decide
infeasible.explain: Whether someone holds the right to decide this approval.

unknown.label: Unknown
unknown.explain: Whether someone holds the right to decide this approval.

eligible.label: You can decide
eligible.explain: Why this is in your inbox.

escalated_backup.label: Overdue: you are the backup
escalated_backup.explain: Why this is in your inbox.

L0.label: Hotfix
L0.explain: An urgent fix that skips planning; a follow-up small change is opened after.

L1.label: Quick fix
L1.explain: The smallest change: spec and a short plan, no research or design.

L2.label: Readiness fix
L2.explain: A fix the factory proposes to close a readiness gap in the repo.

L3.label: Small change
L3.explain: A small change with a short spec and plan, no design step.

L4.label: Feature
L4.explain: A normal feature: research, spec, design, plan, build.

L5.label: Higher-risk feature
L5.explain: A feature with more risk; needs a separate staging environment.

L6.label: Large initiative
L6.explain: A large piece of work whose goal is worked out and signed off first.

L7.label: Experiment
L7.explain: A throwaway build to answer a question; ends in a report, never a PR.

L8.label: Done by a person
L8.explain: A person does the work; the factory still checks and records it.

R1.label: Moved to a bigger track
R1.explain: The work turned out bigger; steps were added. No approval needed.

R2.label: Moved to a lighter track
R2.explain: The work is smaller than thought; needs "Allow a lighter track".

R3.label: Agents paused on this track
R3.explain: Too many items failed on this track; new work goes to a person until reset.

R4.label: Hotfix follow-up
R4.explain: The hotfix is done; a follow-up small change makes it permanent.

census.label: Read only
census.explain: Agents may read the repo and plan, run experiments, and support people's own work; no agent code.

light.label: Small changes
light.explain: Agents may also make small changes, hotfixes and readiness fixes.

full.label: All work
full.explain: Agents may also build features and large initiatives.

T0.label: Low risk
T0.explain: No production use and no real data; the owner confirms it.

T2.label: High risk
T2.explain: Production, money or personal data; more approvals and two people.

A0.label: Agents propose only
A0.explain: Every agent change gets a full human review.

A1.label: Agents assisted
A1.explain: Agents work; every PR gets a full review.

A2.label: Agents trusted
A2.explain: Agents work; low-risk PRs may get a light review.

A3.label: Agents highly trusted
A3.explain: Most PRs get a light review with spot-checks.

C.label: Full review
C.explain: A code owner reviews every line.

E.label: Light review
E.explain: A lighter review; some merges are spot-checked later.

C1.label: Owners and risk
C1.explain: Who owns the repo, its risk tier, and what to do about each gap.

C2.label: Repo facts and instructions
C2.explain: The facts the agent claims about the repo and the instructions agents will get.

C3.label: Code map and tests
C3.explain: The code map, draft specs and the tests that will be locked.

C4.label: GitHub protection and people
C4.explain: Main-branch protection, the GitHub App's access and who decides what.

SECR.label: Secrets found
SECR.explain: Secrets found in the repo or its history, and what was done with each.

BATCH.label: Issues to file
BATCH.explain: Gaps to file as GitHub issues.

X2.label: Onboarding files change
X2.explain: Approve the files the agent wants to add (AGENTS.md, CODEOWNERS, .factory/).

affirm.label: Confirm
affirm.explain: Your answer to one repo fact.

correct.label: Correct
correct.explain: Your answer to one repo fact.

unknown.label: Don't know
unknown.explain: Your answer to one repo fact.

file_issue.label: Fix now (PR or issue)
file_issue.explain: What to do about one gap.

track_only.label: Track
track_only.explain: What to do about one gap.

waive.label: Accept
waive.explain: What to do about one gap.

red.label: Not safe yet
red.explain: The overall result of the read-only scan.

amber.label: Needs fixes
amber.explain: The overall result of the read-only scan.

green.label: Ready
green.explain: The overall result of the read-only scan.

B1.label: Open secret found
B1.explain: A secret in the repo or its history has not been dealt with.

B2.label: Scan incomplete
B2.explain: The security scan did not finish or is out of date.

B3.label: Main branch not protected
B3.explain: The default branch lacks the required protection.

B4.label: GitHub App too powerful
B4.explain: The App holds a permission it must not have, or required checks are wrong.

B5.label: Unsafe workflow
B5.explain: A GitHub workflow could leak secrets to an agent PR.

B6.label: Deploys on merge, undocumented
B6.explain: Merging deploys, but operations are not documented.

B4a.label: GitHub App too powerful
B4a.explain: The App holds a permission it must not have, or required checks are wrong.

B4b.label: GitHub App too powerful
B4b.explain: The App holds a permission it must not have, or required checks are wrong.

B4c.label: GitHub App too powerful
B4c.explain: The App holds a permission it must not have, or required checks are wrong.

protect_main.label: Main branch protected
protect_main.explain: The default branch needs PRs, approval and the factory check.

app_scope.label: App limited to this repo
app_scope.explain: The GitHub App is installed on selected repos only, with the right permissions.

instructions.label: Agent instructions
instructions.explain: Agent instructions exist and are approved.

LF1.label: No open security issues
LF1.explain: No blocking security finding is open.

LF2.label: Main branch protected
LF2.explain: Protection is in force and the factory check is required.

LF3.label: Tests run and pass
LF3.explain: Setup and tests run cleanly in the sandbox.

LF4.label: Agent tooling checked
LF4.explain: Files that run code or grant tools were checked, and isolation was tested.

LF5.label: Agent instructions approved
LF5.explain: A person approved the agent instructions.

LF6.label: Repo facts confirmed
LF6.explain: At least 90% of the repo facts are confirmed or marked unknown.

LF7.label: Operations documented
LF7.explain: Whether a merge deploys is known and written down.

LF8.label: Network needs declared
LF8.explain: Outside hosts the tests need are listed.

app.label: Waiting for the GitHub App
app.explain: Install the factory's GitHub App on this repo to start.

card.label: Needs your review
card.explain: The summary is ready for you.

blocked.label: Blocked
blocked.explain: Something must be fixed on GitHub before the agent can go on.

starter.label: Needs starter files
starter.explain: The repo needs basic files first; the agent proposes them.

parked.label: Paused: no answer
parked.explain: Nobody answered for 5 working days. Resume when ready.

done.label: Onboarded
done.explain: The repo is signed off at its level.

rejected.label: Sign-off refused
rejected.explain: The sign-off was refused; fix and ask again.

superseded.label: Replaced
superseded.explain: A newer onboarding replaced this one.

VRL.label: Testing
VRL.explain: Can agents check their own work.

ERL.label: Environment
ERL.explain: Can the code be built and run safely.

ORL.label: Operations
ORL.explain: Is it known how changes reach production.

KRL.label: Knowledge
KRL.explain: What agents are told and can read about the repo.

reaffirm.label: Confirm again
reaffirm.explain: What a change since onboarding means.

suspend.label: Agents suspended
suspend.explain: What a change since onboarding means.

security.label: Security check needed
security.explain: What a change since onboarding means.

affirmed.label: Approved
affirmed.explain: The state of a file the factory placed.

pending_projection.label: Waiting for PR merge
pending_projection.explain: The state of a file the factory placed.

drift.label: Changed on GitHub
drift.explain: The state of a file the factory placed.

absent.label: Missing
absent.explain: The state of a file the factory placed.

correct.label: Correct
correct.explain: Questions that test what the agent learned about the repo.

incorrect.label: Incorrect
incorrect.explain: Questions that test what the agent learned about the repo.

unsure.label: Unsure
unsure.explain: Questions that test what the agent learned about the repo.

observed.label: As found
observed.explain: A draft spec from the code, or confirmed as intended behaviour.

intended.label: As intended
intended.explain: A draft spec from the code, or confirmed as intended behaviour.

Clarifying.label: Questions asked
Clarifying.explain: The factory asked questions; answer them to go on.

S1.label: Intake
S1.explain: The stage the work is in now.

S2.label: Research
S2.explain: The stage the work is in now.

S3.label: Spec
S3.explain: The stage the work is in now.

S4.label: Design
S4.explain: The stage the work is in now.

S5.label: Plan
S5.explain: The stage the work is in now.

Scheduling.label: Queued for build
Scheduling.explain: The plan is approved; waiting for a coding slot.

S6.label: Build
S6.explain: The stage the work is in now.

S7.label: Verify
S7.explain: The stage the work is in now.

G4.label: In code review
G4.explain: Waiting for a code owner to approve the PR.

S8a.label: Merge
S8a.explain: The stage the work is in now.

S8b.label: Release
S8b.explain: The stage the work is in now.

S9.label: Close
S9.explain: The stage the work is in now.

G6.label: Waiting for your acceptance
G6.explain: Done; the requester must accept it.

Held.label: On hold
Held.explain: Paused for a reason shown beside it.

Handoff.label: Needs a person
Handoff.explain: The agents stopped; a person must choose what happens next.

Quarantined.label: Security hold
Quarantined.explain: Stopped after unsafe agent behaviour; security decides next.

Parked.label: Waiting for answers
Parked.explain: Paused until the questions are answered; ends after 5 working days.

Declined.label: Declined
Declined.explain: The factory will not do this request.

HandedOverClosed.label: Closed by a person
HandedOverClosed.explain: A person took the work over and closed it.

Parked.label: Waiting for answers
Parked.explain: Paused until the questions are answered; ends after 5 working days.

Blocked.label: Blocked: environment
Blocked.explain: The tests fail before any change, or the sandbox is broken; fix and retry.

ReleaseHeld.label: Release on hold
ReleaseHeld.explain: The release was refused; fix and ask again, or open a new item.

SpikeReport.label: Experiment report
SpikeReport.explain: The experiment finished; read its report.

DESK.label: Needs a person
DESK.explain: Items waiting for a person to take over or choose.

BIN.label: Declined
BIN.explain: Requests the factory will not do.

working.label: Working
working.explain: What the item is doing now on the floor.

waiting.label: Waiting
waiting.explain: What the item is doing now on the floor.

held.label: On hold
held.explain: What the item is doing now on the floor.

stuck.label: Stuck
stuck.explain: No sign of life from the agent for longer than the set time.

done.label: Done
done.explain: What the item is doing now on the floor.

declined.label: Declined
declined.explain: What the item is doing now on the floor.

B1.label: Needs more information
B1.explain: Questions asked; up to 2 rounds, then paused 5 working days.

B2.label: Goal unclear
B2.explain: Research found the goal unclear; the goal is confirmed again (2 tries, then a person).

B3.label: Spec failed checks
B3.explain: The spec failed validation; the agent retries (3 tries).

B4.label: Design found a spec gap
B4.explain: The design shows the spec is missing something; back to spec once.

B5.label: Plan changes requested
B5.explain: The plan was sent back; after 2 times, a person writes the plan.

B6.label: Blocked: environment
B6.explain: Tests fail before any change; the build waits until the environment is fixed.

B7.label: Checks failing, retrying
B7.explain: The agent's own checks fail; it retries within its limits.

B8.label: Out of scope: re-plan
B8.explain: The change went beyond its part; the part is split and approved again.

B9.label: Fixing check findings
B9.explain: Verify found something fixable; the agent fixes it.

B10.label: Spec unclear
B10.explain: Verify found the spec ambiguous; the spec is approved again once.

B11.label: Wrong approach: re-plan
B11.explain: Verify found the approach wrong; the plan is approved again once.

B12.label: Locked test must change
B12.explain: A locked test must change; needs "Change a locked test".

B13.label: Changes requested in review
B13.explain: The code owner requested changes; up to 2 rounds.

B14.label: Reviewer unsure
B14.explain: A light reviewer was unsure; a code owner does a full review.

B15.label: Base branch moved
B15.explain: The main branch moved; checks run again (2 times).

B16.label: Deploy unhealthy: rolled back
B16.explain: The release was rolled back; a new fix item was opened.

B17.label: Bug found after merge
B17.explain: A problem was found after merge; a new fix item was opened.

B18.label: Result not accepted
B18.explain: The requester did not accept the result; a new linked item was opened.

B19.label: Spot-check found a miss
B19.explain: An audit found a missed problem; too many suspend light reviews.

B20.label: Scope changed
B20.explain: The requester changed the scope; back to spec (once).

B21.label: Decision overdue
B21.explain: Waited over 1 working day; sent to the backup approver. Never approved automatically.

B22.label: Not eligible
B22.explain: The request does not fit this repo or the factory.
